speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you presented with an episode of loss of consciousness; to begin my assessment, could you describe exactly what happened right before you passed out, and were you able to speak to anyone during the event?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the loss of consciousness occurring immediately after voiding is a very specific clue. Given your age and the sudden nature of the event, do you have a known history of high blood pressure or heart disease, and were you taking any medications before this happened?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episode of loss of consciousness. I also have Regained consciousness quickly without confusion, No urinary incontinence, No bite marks or injuries.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Vasovagal Syncope secondary to micturition (micturition syncope).

This diagnosis is supported by the classic presentation of loss of consciousness immediately following urination, rapid recovery without confusion, and the absence of trauma or incontinence.
